reviews.decision_reason: map_coverage preserves the upstream needs window, maps exact need text to declared capabilities, and emits direct coverage only when a capability_id exists; unmatched needs remain unsupported. The observed final coverage matches this behavior, so this boundary is not the root cause.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: map exact capability coverage without generic keyword matching

reviews.decision_reason: prioritize_needs reverses the unsupported flag: it sets unsupported to true when coverage == 'direct'. The final priorities then rank covered needs n06-r02 through n06-r06 and n06-r08 ahead of actually unsupported needs n06-r01 and n06-r07, causing the recommendation to prioritize an already covered need. This is the top behaviorally significant root cause.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: rank unsupported needs before covered needs
use upstream provenance rank within each group
avoid unrelated or already covered candidates as demand priorities

reviews.decision_reason: synthesize_recommendation retains the eight-item priority window and derives the recommendation from the first already-ranked priority. The bad recommendation is downstream of the inverted unsupported flag from prioritize_needs, not introduced here.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: construct recommendation from first ranked record

reviews.decision_reason: select_demand_records keeps the supplied demanded corpus rows using the score threshold and explicit fallback ids. In this package all eight rows qualify and are preserved for downstream review; no generic keyword demand inference is introduced here.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: select demanded corpus rows from supplied evidence only

reviews.decision_reason: normalize_evidence reindexes to the required columns, applies neutral missing-field sentinels, coerces numeric fields, filters to the allowed record window, and retains the eight supplied needs. No contradictory evidence indicates loss or fabrication at this boundary.

assemble_provenance builds ranked evidence-source rows from normalized needs and ranks them by demand_score descending with record_id tie-breaks. The downstream handoff hashes for needs and evidence_sources match the upstream producer hashes, so this boundary is reusable for reporting.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: build provenance records from normalized needs
preserve exact handoff material for downstream
